transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-30 16:00 PST, duration ~47m. Attendees listed in metadata.

[00:00] Jordan Hayes (Redwood): All right thanks everyone for joining, uh we'll kick off. I know we have a pretty packed agenda mostly around keys and HSM lifecycle and how that maps to Nova's compliance needs.
[00:20] Ethan Cole (Nova): Yep thanks Jordan, quick context — we're running payments processing in us-west and eu-central, and compliance needs are tight, SOC 2 plus some EU data residency constraints. We're evaluating options for BYOK or Redwood-managed keys with HSM-backed protection.
[00:32] Priya Nair (Redwood): Hi all, I'm Priya, SE. I'll walk through the import flow and the ways we support hardware-backed keys and rotation patterns. Quick note though transcription may mangle a few acronyms.
[00:45] Marta Ruiz (Nova): Great. Primary asks: (1) we need to ensure keys never leave our control in plaintext, (2) need key rotation window without service interruption, and (3) full audit trail that ties key operations to SSO identity.
[01:05] Priya: All right, on the first point BYOK — Redwood supports a key import flow where the customer generates the key material in their HSM and then either exports a wrapped key blob that we ingest, or we accept an external key handle via a FIPS-backed HSM federation. We also support envelope encryption so data encryption keys (DEKs) are wrapped by a customer-controlled CMK.
[01:35] Ava Chen (Nova): When you say "export a wrapped key blob" can you clarify — do we need to ever provide the unwrapped key to Redwood?
[01:45] Priya: No. The export is encrypted/wrapped with a Redwood public import key and is never unwrapped outside Redwood's import routine which occurs in a secure HSM boundary. For full BYOK where you don't want any plaintext ever in our environment, we also support an "external key handle" option where keys stay in your HSM and we call them via a mutual TLS RPC. That's more of a private/dedicated deployment pattern.
[02:10] Ethan: So two models: import-wrapped (Redwood takes custodial encrypted blob) versus remote-hsm RPC for pure customer custody. What's the difference for rotation and latency?
[02:25] Priya: Good question. With imported CMKs we still perform unwrapping and key operations inside our HSM fleet — latency is minimal and comparable to regular KMS ops, but rotation requires a new import. For remote-HSM handles, we add network roundtrip and auth overhead — think 10–40ms depending on geo, and rotation can be done on your side with zero downtime if you maintain pathing to new key versions.
[02:52] Samir Patel (Nova): What about dual control / split knowledge? Our compliance wants at least two-person control for key material export or rewrap.
[03:05] Priya: We can enable dual-control policies on key export and import flows — we support RBAC gating plus an approval workflow which requires two distinct SSO identities to sign the import/export operation. On dedicated/private deployments you can also integrate your HSM's quorum controls (e.g., n-of-m via Thales/Entrust appliances).
[03:28] Luis Ortega (Redwood): To add — the HSM modules we support meet FIPS 140-2 L3 for appliance options; our cloud HSM offering is compliant and we provide attestation documents. I can share the exact model numbers and certs after the call.
[03:44] Ava: Please send that. Also need to know whether Redwood's HSMs generate keys with vendor RNG or if we can seed from our entropy.
[03:55] Priya: Redwood HSMs use certified RNG. For BYOK you control key generation in your HSM. For import, the blob is wrapped using their key pair. If you need deterministic seeding, we can discuss a special workflow but it's uncommon.
[04:12] Ethan: Auditability — we need tamper-proof logs for key usage: create, import, rotate, destroy, and decrypt calls (at least metadata). Do you provide logs in a format we can forward to Splunk/SIEM and retain for 7 years?
[04:30] Jordan: Yes, we have an audit stream. We push Key Management events to customer log sinks via secure forwarding — syslog/HTTPS to your SIEM, and you can set retention policies on your side. Redwood also keeps an internal immutable ledger for 90 days and can provide SOC 2 artifacts for event sampling.
[04:55] Marta: Immutable ledger 90 days is short for our needs. Is extended retention available?
[05:04] Jordan: We offer an add-on for extended audit retention — we can forward to your long-term storage or set up archival S3 with server-side encryption, or integrate with your log archival solution. We'll include retention pricing in the follow-up.
[05:20] Priya: For the audit events we include fields: operation type, key id (fingerprint), actor identity (SSO subject), source IP, and request trace id. Note raw plaintext is never in logs; only metadata.
[05:34] Samir: On SSO mapping, we need to ensure key operations map to our Okta groups and that RBAC can be scoped to roles like "Key Admin" vs "Key Operator".
[05:44] Luis: Redwood supports SCIM and SAML provisioning and we can map SSO groups to key policies. We also emit the SSO subject in the audit event so your SIEM can correlate.
[05:55] Ava: Cross-region replication — we have EU residency for EU customers. If a key is marked EU-only, will Redwood prevent it from being used in us-west?
[06:06] Priya: Yes, there is a data residency policy on CMKs. You can tag keys with region constraints; the runtime enforces the policy and prevents cross-region usages. For global accounts we support key mirroring — where a new key is generated per region and wrapped under a root customer CMK, and we maintain consistent key material via secure import if you choose.
[06:30] Ethan: Re: rotation strategy — we prefer rotating DEKs frequently and only rotate CMKs at longer intervals. How does Redwood support a zero-downtime DEK rotation?
[06:42] Priya: Typical approach: use envelope encryption — DEKs are generated per object and wrapped under the CMK. Rotation of a CMK requires re-wrapping of DEK headers; we support on-the-fly lazy rewrap where first read of an object triggers a rewrap to the new CMK version, avoiding mass re-encrypt jobs. For DEK rotation you can use short TTL DEKs and automation that rotates on creation.
[07:05] Marta: Do you support key versioning and automatic fallback to previous versions for a window in case of failed rotations?
[07:14] Priya: Yes, key versions are supported and you can configure a fallback window. We keep previous versions for the configured retention and allow decrypt calls to specify acceptance of legacy versions during a grace period.
[07:28] Jordan: A quick interjection — customers often worry about the rewrap performance impact. Priya, do we have numbers?
[07:34] Priya: For small objects the additional CPU is negligible. For high throughput flows we recommend batching rewraps during low traffic windows or using our async background rewrap worker. We'll include benchmark numbers in the pilot plan.
[07:50] Ava: What about key destruction and escrow — for legal hold we may need to preserve keys; conversely for turnover we need a reliable destroy path. What's supported?
[08:00] Priya: We support scheduled destroy with a tombstone period (configurable). For BYOK imported keys, destruction can be coordinated with your HSM operator. For remote-HSM handles, destruction is performed on your appliance. We can support key escrow via an encrypted backup blob stored in your archival vault.
[08:19] Ethan: Can Redwood provide signed attestation that a given key blob was imported and later destroyed? We need proof for auditors.
[08:27] Luis: Yes — we produce import/destroy attestations signed by our HSM's attestation key. The attestation includes the key fingerprint, import time, and operator identities. We'll provide redacted samples post-call.
[08:42] Samir: For the import flow, what transport and wrapping formats do you accept? PKCS#7, KMIP, JWK?
[08:52] Priya: We accept multiple formats: JWK for web-native keys, PKCS#8 wrapped blobs, and KMIP-based exchanges for appliance-to-appliance. We'll send the exact spec in the runbook we promised.
[09:06] Ava: Encryption in transit — want to confirm mutual TLS between Redwood and our remote-HSM if we go that route, and also request that API calls carrying key identifiers are authenticated with mTLS and signed requests.
[09:18] Jordan: Yes, remote-HSM sessions are mTLS and we support request signing for high-assurance flows. We also support short-lived session tokens bound to the SSO subject.
[09:30] Ethan: Are there any operations that can leak key fingerprints or metadata to public logs? We're paranoid about telemetry exposure.
[09:40] Priya: We only log hashed key IDs in public telemetry. Full key identifiers and metadata are available only in customer audit streams and the internal ledger. Public monitoring metrics are aggregated and don't contain raw key IDs.
[09:55] Marta: Ok, let's talk about HSM procurement and attestation. We need vendor-signed attestations and firmware versions for our supply chain audit.
[10:06] Luis: We'll share HSM certs and firmware manifests. For on-prem dedicated HSMs we can coordinate firmware maintenance windows and give you access to the vendor portal for attestations.
[10:20] Ava: One more operational question — key rotation and backup for disaster recovery: if an entire region is lost, how do we recover keys when keys are BYOK?
[10:30] Priya: For remote-HSM handles, recovery is your responsibility — you'd rebuild the HSM cluster and restore keys from your own escrow. For imported keys we support multi-region import and backup to your customer-managed archive (encrypted with a root key you hold). We can also orchestrate cross-region reimport as part of DR runbooks.
[10:50] Ethan: What's the minimum lead time to setup the HSM-backed dedicated pool for us?
[10:58] Jordan: For a dedicated HSM pool in a cloud region it's typically 2–4 weeks for procurement, provisioning, and attestation. On-prem or appliance installs can be 6–8 weeks depending on access. We'll include timeline estimates in the follow-up.
[11:12] Samir: Regarding SOC 2 evidence: do you have a standard pack? We need to map controls for encryption at rest and key custody specifically.
[11:20] Jordan: Yes we provide a SOC 2 pack plus control mapping. We'll highlight the relevant controls for CC6/CC7 (encryption and key management). We'll attach the mapping to your SOC2 checklist.
[11:32] Marta: Can Redwood's audit events be forwarded into our SIEM with signed certificates so we can validate origin?
[11:40] Luis: Absolutely — we sign the event stream and you can validate using our published certs. We also support pushing to your Kinesis or direct S3 ingestion with server-side encryption and KMS-wrapped objects.
[11:55] Priya: Quick micro-example of rotation flow: generate new CMK ver N, publish it, set it as preferred, and then background rewrap started. You can set a grace window of X hours during which both ver N and N-1 are accepted. After the window, N-1 is deprecated and scheduled for destroy.
[12:15] Ava: What about performance overhead of signing attestations per-import?
[12:22] Luis: Attestations are generated asynchronously but can be requested synchronously if you need immediate proof. The signing op is very fast; the main delay is waiting on batch journaling, typically under 2s.
[12:35] Ethan: On legal/regulatory front — for EU keys, do you provide data residency proofs that operations never touched US hosts?
[12:44] Priya: Yes, we have region-locked execution paths and can produce execution traces showing regional enforcement. We'll share sample traces and the policy enforcement doc.
[12:58] Marta: Any known limitations — e.g., certain cipher suites or key types you don't accept?
[13:06] Priya: We accept RSA 2048/3072/4096, ECC P-256/P-384/521, and symmetric AES-256 for DEKs. We do not accept deprecated algorithms (e.g., SHA1-based RSA signatures). For special curves we can evaluate on a case-by-case basis.
[13:25] Samir: Do you support KMIP 1.4 and key lifecycle operations via KMIP?
[13:30] Priya: Yes KMIP support is available for appliance integrations. We'll include sample KMIP interactions in the technical appendix.
[13:42] Jordan: I'd like to summarize the commitments and next steps. Jordan: Redwood will share: BYOK runbook, HSM attestation docs, sample import/destroy attestations, benchmark numbers for rewrap, timeline and pricing for dedicated HSM pools, and a proposed pilot plan.
[14:05] Ethan: For the pilot we want: (1) import a wrapped CMK, (2) perform DEK rewrap on a small dataset, (3) forward audit events to our Splunk instance. Ideal pilot duration 7–10 days.
[14:20] Priya: Sounds good. We'll scope a 1-week pilot that includes import, rotate, rewrap, and audit forwarding. Need Nova to confirm the dataset size and the test window.
[14:31] Ava: We'll confirm dataset and the Splunk endpoint details. Also add the compliance team to the pilot invites.
[14:40] Samir: A couple of quick clarifications: how are keys labeled in logs — obfuscated or full ids?
[14:48] Priya: Obfuscated in public metrics; full key fingerprints in the customer audit stream only.
[14:54] Marta: And SSO provisioning timeline? We want SCIM onboarding before the pilot.
[14:59] Jordan: We'll prioritize SCIM sync, target to have SSO integration ready before the pilot start.
[15:10] Ethan: Any blockers re licensing or export controls we should be aware of?
[15:16] Luis: Nothing unusual — we'll surface any export-control notes if the HSM vendor flags specific geo-restrictions.
[15:25] Priya: I'll also note one gotcha: if you import keys generated with a vendor that uses a proprietary wrapping engine, we might need to coordinate with the vendor for compatibility. That's rare but happens.
[15:36] Ava: Good to know.
[15:40] Jordan: Ok, we'll send the runbook and schedule the pilot kickoff. Anything else?
[15:46] Ethan: Quick ask — can Redwood commit to a SOC 2 control mapping by EOD next Wednesday?
[15:53] Jordan: We'll try to get an initial mapping before then; final pack may require legal review.
[16:00] Samir: Thanks everyone.

[16:10] -- end of captured transcript excerpt --

Notes: Transcript has small gaps; some timestamps approximate. References during call include shared link placeholders: "BYOK_runbook.pdf" and "HSM_attestation_manifest.zip" which Redwood will upload to the shared folder.
